goldens.comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.
goldens.reasoning: C1 points out the same race: the lazy @loaded_locales init has no synchronization.

goldens.comment: Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).
goldens.reasoning: C2 raises the same String vs Symbol normalization problem, which leads to a second load of the same locale.

candidates: `@loaded_locales ||= []` is not protected by `LOAD_MUTEX`, introducing a race condition. Two threads could simultaneously see `nil`, each create a new array, and one write is lost. Consider removing the lazy init and relying on `load_locale` (which already guards access with `LOAD_MUTEX`) directly, or wrapping this in the mutex.

`locale` is not normalized to a Symbol (or String) before the `include?` check. In Ruby `:en != "en"`, so passing a String when the locale was previously loaded as a Symbol (from `I18n.config.locale`) will bypass the guard and trigger a redundant load. Consider adding `locale = locale.to_sym` at the top of the method.
Preserve standard locale-ancestor fallbacks here; otherwise regional locales skip matching base-language translations.
